title: Volume 5 · Month-End and Year-End Close
subtitle: Lessons 5–8: the pre-close checks, the closing voucher, the month-end pack and the move from FY2026 into FY2027
outcomes: Run five pre-close checks that catch ninety per cent of month-end problems
Close a period with the closing voucher and explain what it locks
Assemble a month-end pack a business owner can read in five minutes
Carry balances into a new fiscal year without losing an opening entry

slides.title: Five checks before anyone closes anything
bullets: Closing a period with unposted documents is the single most common month-end failure
Control accounts must agree with their subledgers before the trial balance is printed
Stock value, bank reconciliation and SST liability each have one owner and one proof
Run the checks on the last working day, not after the close, or the fixes cost a week

rows: Filter status Draft on sales and purchase documents
Debtors and Creditors against the control accounts
Stock Balance and SST liability account
Worksheet with five ticks and a name

slides.notes: Write these five on a card and give it to the client's finance lead, because the consultant will not be there every month. The order matters: draft documents first, then control accounts, then bank, then stock and tax. Each check has a named owner in the worksheet, and the close does not start until all five are ticked.

slides.title: What each pre-close check proves
bullets: Each check answers one question, and a pass means the question is closed
A control account difference of even one cent blocks the close, because it compounds
Draft documents are not errors until they are explained, but unexplained they are
The SST liability must equal the output tax on submitted invoices, not on draft ones
slides.notes: Two figures here deserve rehearsal: debtors of thirteen thousand two hundred, which is twelve thousand of sales plus one thousand two hundred of tax, and the SST payable of exactly one thousand two hundred. If either is off, the mistake is almost always a document without tax or a tax row with the wrong account, and both show up in the tax summary long before an auditor finds them.

slides.title: Close the period with the closing voucher
bullets: The Period Closing Voucher is the document you create; it posts the closing entries and marks the period reported
Submitting it enqueues Process Period Closing Voucher jobs, one per chunk, and those do the actual posting
Watch GL Entry Processing Status move to Completed before you trust any figure in the pack
A failed chunk writes into Error Message, and Accounts Settings carries a legacy controller switch for that case
Close after the pack is produced and signed, never before, because closing restricts later changes

rows: Account that receives the closing entries

slides.notes: Net profit of four thousand six hundred eighty is sales of twelve thousand less cost of goods of six thousand, freight of sixty, accrual of eight hundred, insurance of one hundred and stock adjustment of three hundred sixty. Make the learner compute it before the close. Then teach the two documents properly: the Period Closing Voucher is yours to create, and the Process Period Closing Voucher rows are the background jobs that post it, so GL Entry Processing Status is the field you watch before anyone signs the pack.

slides.title: What the close does, and what it refuses
bullets: The close zeroes income and expense accounts and leaves balance sheet accounts alone
It does not validate your arithmetic, so a wrong profit is simply transferred
It restricts later changes to the period, which is the point of closing at all
Stock value and party balances must be correct before the voucher, not after

rows: refused with a period validation message

slides.notes: A learner who expects the close to catch their mistakes will close a wrong month and then argue with the auditor. Say it plainly: the close is a bookend, not a review. The review is the five checks that come before it, and the arithmetic of net profit of four thousand six hundred eighty is the test that the review worked.

slides.title: From FY2026 into FY2027 without losing a balance
bullets: Year end closes the profit and loss, and every balance sheet account carries forward
The opening entry is generated by the close, not typed by hand
Lock the old year after the accounts are filed, and keep the audit trail intact
Confirm the opening balance sheet against the last reported one before you allow any entry
slides.notes: The year-end conversation is a governance conversation, so bring the freezing date and the audit trail rather than a checklist. The test is simple: can you produce the 31-12-2026 balance sheet a year later, unchanged? If a backdated entry can still post, the answer is no, and that is a finding the client's auditor will raise.

slides.title: Month-end pack, one page per statement
bullets: The pack must be readable by an owner who will not open the system
Every figure on the page has a report behind it, named in the same row
Variances are explained in words, not left for the reader to guess
The pack is signed and dated, because it is the evidence of the close

rows: How much cash is tied up
Who owes us and whom do we owe

slides.notes: Five pages, five owners, one signature: that is a month-end pack a client will actually use. Anything longer is a data dump, and anything shorter invites the question the consultant cannot answer in the meeting. Build it once as a template, then let the client's finance lead own it by month three, with the consultant reviewing rather than producing.

slides.title: Close calendar with owners and evidence
bullets: A close calendar is a contract, and every row needs a name and a proof
Working day three is the practical limit for a distributor of this size
The consultant's job is to build the calendar and then leave it behind
Every task produces one artefact, and the artefacts are the audit file

rows: Cut off sales, delivery notes and receipts
Receive all supplier invoices into the system
Close the period and produce the pack

slides.notes: Give the client this calendar before go-live, not in the first month end, because it forces the ownership conversation while everyone is still enthusiastic. If a task has no owner, the close will slip, and the consultant will end up producing the pack from memory at eleven at night. That is the pattern to design out.

lab.title: Lab · Run the checks, close January and produce the pack
steps: Print the January trial balance and confirm debits equal credits
Reconcile debtors and creditors control accounts against their subledgers
Confirm the bank reconciliation difference is 0.00 and list timing items
Compute net profit for January from the five known adjustments
Close the period with a closing voucher dated 31-01-2026
Confirm retained earnings moves by 4,680.00 and the P and L resets
Attempt a backdated journal and record the validation message
Produce the five-page pack and name the source report for each figure
lab.done: Done when January is closed, net profit of 4,680.00 sits in retained earnings, a backdated entry is refused, and every figure in the pack names the report it came from.

quiz.question: What should happen before a period is closed?
options: Run the five pre-close checks and sign them off
quiz.why: Draft documents, control accounts, bank, stock and tax must all be proved before closing, otherwise the reported figures are wrong from the start.

quiz.question: January sales are 12,000.00 with 10 % SST. What is the SST payable?
quiz.why: Output tax is 10 % of the taxable sales of 12,000.00, giving 1,200.00, which is a liability rather than income.

quiz.question: What does the closing voucher do?
options: Transfers profit and loss balances to retained earnings
quiz.why: Closing transfers the period's income and expense balances to retained earnings and marks the period as reported.

quiz.question: Sales 12,000.00 and costs of 6,000.00 plus 60.00 freight, 800.00 accrual, 100.00 insurance and 360.00 stock adjustment leave net profit of what?
Why set a frozen accounts date after filing?
options: To refuse backdated entries into a reported year
quiz.why: A frozen date prevents postings into a year whose statements are already reported and filed, preserving the audit trail.

memory.spine: Close in one order: fix what moves, then judge, then calculate, and only then lock the period so nobody can edit it.

device.label: Move, judge, calculate, lock
expansion: Cash: reconcile the bank statement to the ledger before anything else
Count: reconcile stock and clear negative quantities
Judge: accruals and prepayments for costs incurred but not yet billed
Calculate: depreciation and any valuation repost
Lock: the Period Closing Voucher posts the closing entries and marks the period reported

cards.q: What is the most common month end failure?
cards.a: Closing with unposted documents: drafts, unallocated payments and negative stock.

cards.q: What does the Period Closing Voucher actually do?
cards.a: It zeroes income and expense accounts into the closing account and leaves balance sheet accounts alone.

cards.q: Can a document be edited in a closed period?
cards.a: Not without reopening or correcting in the next period. The close is a lock, not a label.

cards.q: At year end, what carries forward?
cards.a: Every balance sheet balance, while the profit and loss closes into equity.
Every row of the close calendar needs an owner and a proof, and the pack must read without the system.

trap.what: The period is closed to stop people posting, before anything is reconciled.
trap.why: The voucher locks in whatever was wrong and every later report inherits it, so the correction costs twice the work.

narration: Month end is a process, not an event, and the consultant who builds the process is the one who gets invited back. Five checks come first: the trial balance, the draft documents, the debtors and creditors control accounts, the bank reconciliation, and stock with tax. When all five are signed, the close can start. January carries twelve thousand of sales, six thousand of cost, and four thousand six hundred eighty of net profit once freight, accrual, insurance and the stock adjustment are counted. The closing voucher moves that to retained earnings and marks the period as reported. At year end the same discipline carries balances into the new year, and the frozen date stops anyone rewriting a year that has already been filed. A close calendar with a name against every task is what makes the process repeatable, and the signed five-page pack is what makes it auditable. Build both once, hand the ownership to the client's finance lead, and the consultant's job becomes review rather than rescue.
